definition.general: Precipitation is the rain and snow that reach the ground, here as the month's average in millimetres per hour.
definition.expert: GPM IMERG Final monthly precipitation rate (satellite retrieval, gauge-adjusted), mm/hr.

definition.general: This is how warm the air near the ground is, computed by a land model that is fed with observations.
definition.expert: GLDAS-2.1 Noah near-surface air temperature (forcing field of the land surface model), K, shown as °C.

definition.general: Soil moisture is the water held in the top 10 cm of soil, in kilograms per square metre.
definition.expert: GLDAS-2.1 Noah soil moisture content, 0–10 cm layer (land surface model), kg m-2.

gldas_evap.name: Evapotranspiration
gldas_evap.short: water going back into the air

definition.general: Evapotranspiration is how fast water returns to the air: evaporation from soil and water, plus water given off by leaves.
definition.expert: GLDAS-2.1 Noah evapotranspiration flux (land surface model), kg m-2 s-1.

definition.general: This is the air temperature near the ground as an infrared instrument on a satellite reads it, at about 1:30 pm local time.
definition.expert: AIRS Level 3 surface air temperature, ascending (daytime, about 13:30 local) overpass (satellite retrieval), K, shown as °C.

definition.general: Total water vapor is all the vapor in the air above one square metre of ground, counted as kilograms of water.
definition.expert: AIRS Level 3 total column water vapor (satellite retrieval), kg/m2.

merra2_t2m.name: 2 m air temperature
merra2_t2m.short: air temperature 2 m above the ground

definition.general: This is the air temperature 2 metres above the ground, computed by NASA's MERRA-2, which blends worldwide observations with a weather model.
definition.expert: MERRA-2 reanalysis 2 m air temperature (T2M), K, shown as °C.

definition.general: This is the amount of nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), a gas given off when fuel burns, in the lowest layer of the atmosphere.
definition.expert: OMI tropospheric NO₂ vertical column density (satellite retrieval), molecules/cm^2.

definition.general: Total ozone is all the ozone in the air above a place, in Dobson units (DU); most of it sits high up in the ozone layer.
definition.expert: OMI total column ozone (satellite retrieval), Dobson units (DU).

definition.general: The UV aerosol index shows how much dust and smoke that absorb ultraviolet light are in the air; it has no unit.
definition.expert: OMI UV aerosol index (satellite retrieval), unitless; responds mainly to UV-absorbing aerosols and their height.

definition.general: Vegetation greenness (NDVI) is how green the land looks from space: near 1 for dense plants, near 0 for bare ground or cities.
definition.expert: MODIS Terra NDVI, (NIR − red) / (NIR + red) (satellite retrieval), unitless.

definition.general: Land surface temperature is how hot the ground itself is (not the air), as a satellite reads it at about 10:30 am local time.
definition.expert: MODIS Terra daytime land surface temperature, about 10:30 local overpass (satellite retrieval), K, shown as °C.

definition.general: This is the air temperature a thermometer at a weather station measured, averaged over the month.
definition.expert: NOAA GHCNh station air temperature, monthly mean of daily means (in situ), °C.

power_t2m.name: 2 m air temperature (NASA POWER)
power_t2m.short: air temperature 2 m above the ground

definition.general: This is the air temperature 2 metres above the ground from the same MERRA-2 data, obtained through the NASA POWER service.
definition.expert: NASA POWER 2 m air temperature (MERRA-2 reanalysis), °C.

definition.general: Land surface temperature is how hot the ground itself is (not the air), as a satellite reads it at about 10:30 am local time.
definition.expert: MODIS Terra daytime land surface temperature via Planetary Computer (satellite retrieval), K, shown as °C.

definition.general: Vegetation greenness (NDVI) is how green the land looks from space: near 1 for dense plants, near 0 for bare ground or cities.
definition.expert: MODIS Terra NDVI, 250 m 16-day composites via Planetary Computer (satellite retrieval), unitless.
